python.q: In NumPy, what does broadcasting let you do?
o: Run code on several CPU cores
Combine arrays of different shapes by stretching size-1 dimensions
Send an array over the network
python.why: Broadcasting applies an operation across arrays of compatible shapes without copying data, for example adding a row vector to every row of a matrix.

python.q: Which Pandas expression returns only the rows where the column age is greater than 30?
python.why: df['age'] > 30 builds a boolean mask, and indexing the DataFrame with that mask keeps the matching rows.

python.q: What does [x * x for x in range(4)] evaluate to?
python.why: range(4) yields 0, 1, 2, 3, and each value is squared.

python.q: Why use a virtual environment for a Python project?
o: It isolates the project's dependencies from other projects
It is required to import NumPy
python.why: Each project gets its own package versions, which avoids conflicts and makes setups reproducible.

o: The mean score for each team
The team with the highest score
A copy of the DataFrame sorted by team
python.why: groupby splits the rows by team, then mean is computed on the score column within each group.

math.q: What does the gradient of a function point toward?
math.why: The gradient points uphill. Gradient descent steps in the opposite direction to reduce the loss.

math.q: You multiply a 2x3 matrix by a 3x4 matrix. What is the shape of the result?
math.why: The inner dimensions (3 and 3) must match and disappear, leaving the outer dimensions 2x4.

math.q: Which rule of calculus makes backpropagation possible?
math.why: A network is a composition of functions, and the chain rule multiplies local derivatives layer by layer.

o: How far values spread around their mean
math.why: Variance is the average squared distance from the mean.
Bayes' rule updates a prior P(A) with the likelihood P(B|A) after seeing evidence B.

o: The model is too simple to learn the pattern
The model does well on training data but poorly on new data
ml.why: An overfit model memorizes noise in the training set instead of learning patterns that generalize.

ml.q: What is the validation set for?
o: Choosing hyperparameters and models without touching the test set
ml.why: The test set stays untouched until the end so it gives an honest estimate; tuning happens on validation data.

ml.q: For a fraud dataset where 1% of transactions are fraud, which metric is more informative than accuracy?
ml.why: A model that always predicts "not fraud" gets 99% accuracy. Precision and recall show how well the rare class is handled.

o: Penalizes large weights to reduce overfitting
ml.why: L2 adds the sum of squared weights to the loss, which favors smaller weights and smoother models.

ml.q: Why does a random forest usually beat a single deep decision tree?
o: It averages many decorrelated trees, which reduces variance
It uses a neural network internally
ml.why: Averaging trees trained on different samples and feature subsets smooths out individual trees' errors.

o: The gradient of the loss with respect to each parameter
dl.why: It applies the chain rule backward through the network to get every parameter's gradient efficiently.

dl.q: What usually happens if the learning rate is far too high?
dl.why: Large steps overshoot the minimum, so the loss bounces around or blows up.

dl.q: What is the ReLU activation function?
dl.why: ReLU outputs 0 for negative inputs and x for positive inputs. It is cheap and helps avoid vanishing gradients.

o: Normalizes layer activations, which stabilizes and speeds up training
dl.why: Keeping activations well scaled makes deep networks easier to optimize.
Softmax exponentiates the logits and divides by their sum, turning scores into a probability distribution.

transformers.q: In self-attention, how is a token's output computed?
o: As a weighted sum of value vectors, with weights from query-key similarity
By running a convolution over neighbors
transformers.why: Each token's query is compared with every key; softmax turns the scores into weights applied to the values.

transformers.q: Why is the dot product divided by the square root of the key dimension in scaled dot-product attention?
o: To keep scores from growing large and saturating the softmax
transformers.why: Without scaling, large dot products push softmax into regions with tiny gradients.

transformers.q: What does the causal mask in a GPT-style model do?
o: Stops a token from attending to future tokens
transformers.why: Next-token prediction must not peek at the answer, so each position can only see earlier positions.

o: Repeatedly merges frequent symbol pairs to build a subword vocabulary
transformers.why: BPE starts from bytes or characters and merges the most frequent pairs, so common words become single tokens and rare words split into pieces.

transformers.q: Why do transformers need positional information?
o: Attention itself does not know token order
transformers.why: Self-attention treats the input as a set, so positions are added through positional encodings or rotary embeddings.

llm.q: What does setting temperature to 0 usually do?
o: Makes outputs nearly deterministic by favoring the most likely token
llm.why: Low temperature sharpens the token distribution, so the top choice is picked almost every time.

llm.q: What is the most reliable way to get machine-readable output from an LLM in an app?
o: Ask politely for JSON and parse the text
Request a structured output or schema and validate the result in code
llm.why: Schemas plus validation catch malformed output; retries or repair handle the rest.

o: Including a few worked examples in the prompt
Sampling a few times and averaging
llm.why: Examples in the prompt show the format and behavior you want without changing model weights.

llm.q: What is a model's context window?
o: The number of users it can serve
The maximum number of tokens it can consider in one request
The time a request may take
The size of its training set
llm.why: Input plus output tokens must fit in the context window.

o: Small low-rank adapter matrices while the base weights stay frozen
llm.why: LoRA adds small trainable matrices to selected layers, which cuts memory and cost dramatically.

o: Retrains the model on your documents
Retrieves relevant passages and adds them to the prompt before generating
rag.why: The model answers using retrieved context, which keeps knowledge current without retraining.

rag.q: What property do good text embeddings have?
o: Semantically similar text maps to nearby vectors
Every word has the same vector
rag.why: Similarity search over vectors finds passages that mean the same thing even without shared keywords.

rag.q: What tends to go wrong when chunks are too small?
o: Chunks lose surrounding context and become ambiguous
rag.why: A sentence pulled out of context may not answer the question. Overlap or parent-document retrieval helps.

rag.q: Which practice most directly reduces hallucination in a RAG app?
o: Instructing the model to answer only from the retrieved context and to cite sources
rag.why: Grounding instructions plus citations make unsupported claims visible and less likely.

rag.q: How should you evaluate the retrieval step separately from generation?
o: Read a few answers by eye
Measure hit rate or recall at k against questions with known source passages
rag.why: If the right passage is not retrieved, generation cannot succeed, so test retrieval on its own.

agents.q: What is the basic loop of an LLM agent?
o: The model chooses an action, a tool runs it, the result is fed back, repeat until done
agents.why: Agents alternate between model decisions and tool observations until the task is complete or a limit is hit.

o: The model runs code on its own server
The model returns a structured call with arguments and your code executes it
The model edits its own prompt
agents.why: The model only proposes the call. Your application executes it and returns the result.

agents.q: Which is the best safety practice for agents that can take actions?
o: Give them broad permissions to avoid failures
Use least privilege and require human approval for destructive actions
agents.why: Narrow permissions and confirmation steps limit the damage from a wrong or manipulated action.

agents.q: Why set a maximum number of steps on an agent loop?
o: To prevent infinite loops and runaway cost
agents.why: Agents can get stuck retrying. A step budget bounds time, spend, and side effects.

agents.q: What is the Model Context Protocol (MCP)?
o: A file format for model weights
An open protocol for connecting AI apps to tools and data sources
agents.why: MCP standardizes how servers expose tools, resources and prompts so any compatible client can use them.

mlops.q: Why package a model service in a Docker container?
o: It makes the model more accurate
It gives a reproducible runtime that behaves the same in every environment
mlops.why: The container carries the code, dependencies, and configuration, which removes "works on my machine" problems.

o: Production inputs changing so they differ from the training data
mlops.why: When live data no longer resembles the training data, accuracy can silently fall, so monitor input distributions.

mlops.q: Which of these should an LLM app log?
o: Prompts, responses, latency, token usage, and errors
mlops.why: These are the data you need to debug quality, control cost, and spot regressions. Redact sensitive data first.

o: So you can reproduce and roll back behavior
mlops.why: A prompt change can alter outputs as much as a code change, so track and test it the same way.

mlops.q: What is an evaluation set in CI for?
o: Catching quality regressions before a change ships
mlops.why: Running fixed test cases on every change shows whether answers got better or worse.
